title: Coupling and Cohesion
summary: When a service reaches into another object's fields to decide something, a change to that object's representation ripples into every place that read it.
signals: a method in one class reading three or more fields of another class to make a decision
the same interpretation of another object's data duplicated in more than one method or class
a schema or type migration (a field's unit, or a raw string becoming a value type) that forces edits everywhere a collaborator reached into the old shape
long parameter lists or field chains built from a single collaborator's data instead of passing that collaborator

roles.OrderService: collaborator that reaches into another object's data (feature envy)
roles.Customer: object that owns the data — and, after the fix, the behaviour about it
roles.loyaltyDiscount: narrow method, named after the customer's own question, that the collaborator calls instead of reading fields directly
roles.tier / lifetimeSpendMinor / yearsAsMembe: internal representation that should be the owning object's own business
roles.MigratedCustomer / LoyaltyTier: a second representation (tier as a value type) that stands in for a real-world schema migration

stages.title: Feature envy
stages.idea: OrderService reaches into Customer's tier, spend and membership length to price a cancellation, then reads the same fields again for a receipt line. When Customer's tier becomes a value type, OrderService can't reuse either method — it needs a third one just to read the new shape.

stages.title: Behaviour moves to its data
stages.idea: Customer answers its own question — what loyalty discount do I get? — and OrderService collaborates through that one narrow, structurally-typed method. A second Customer representation plugs straight in; OrderService never changes.

checks: What is coupling, and what is cohesion — and how are they different measurements of the same design?
Why does moving the discount rule into Customer lower coupling without making the two classes independent of each other?
Is zero coupling between classes an achievable or even desirable goal? Why or why not?
What is connascence, and how does it make 'coupling' more precise than a single word?
